pk.context: 100 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A PDE5 inhibitor with 41% bioavailability and a nitrate contraindication; the blue diamond tablet is its signature.

clues.text: Rapidly absorbed with a mean absolute bioavailability of 41%; a high-fat meal slows absorption. About 96% is bound to plasma proteins and clearance is mainly hepatic via CYP3A4.
Supplied as the citrate salt, molecular weight 666.7 against 474.6 for the free base. Its solubility in water is 3.5 mg/mL.
Marketed under an NDA as film-coated tablets of 25, 50 and 100 mg.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated with nitrates and with guanylate cyclase stimulators; headache, flushing and dyspepsia are the leading adverse reactions.
Indicated for the treatment of erectile dysfunction.
Inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5, which degrades cGMP, so nitric oxide signaling relaxes smooth muscle for longer; its selectivity over the retinal enzyme PDE6 is only about 10-fold.
The generic name begins with S and has ten letters.
